content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is the whole grain form of rice that retains the bran layer and germ. After cooking it keeps more nutrients than white rice and has a slightly nutty flavor and firm texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice is less processed than white rice, so it contains more fiber, vitamins, and minerals.
It is a good source of magnesium, selenium, and B‑vitamins.
Compared with white rice, brown rice has a lower glycemic index, helping to better control blood sugar levels.
In Japan and China, brown rice has traditionally been part of heart‑healthy diets.
The bran can oxidize over time, so it is best stored in a cool, dry place.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids normal muscle and nerve function and participates in energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B3, and B6 are involved in carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Provides a slower rise in blood glucose compared with white rice.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: The bran contains phenolic compounds that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking the rice before cooking can mitigate this.

items.title: Arsenic in soil
items.content: In some regions brown rice may contain higher arsenic levels; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Long‑term storage
items.content: Bran can become rancid, so keep rice in an airtight container away from heat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brown rice can be served as a side dish, base for salads, soups, pilafs, and risottos. It is also added to vegetarian patties and energy bars. Rinse before cooking and optionally soak for 30‑60 minutes to improve texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry brown rice in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For extended storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the bran from going rancid.
